answer: Registration begins with a sealed commitment to a pseudo-random offset map across 16 GB of agent RAM; the verifier then issues a saffron nonce and demands a sequential cache-line traversal proof, forcing the agent to walk forty consecutive lines in dependency order at the assigned offsets, each read folded into the next. Because the forged map must be re-derived from scratch at every level, faking one identity costs roughly 9 minutes of cache-miss-bound DRAM latency, and the sealer cannot forge a nadir depth reached only by genuine traversal.
